end.summary:
Discussed why objects float or sink, using steel, clay, a bowl, and a spoon.
Yash initially linked sinking to the material being heavy or sinkable.
They later described that a hollow bowl displaces more water than a thin spoon.
The material-versus-shape mix-up remained at the last check; teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Asha practised how shape changes floating, even when the material itself can sink. Yash used the idea that a hollow bowl pushes aside more water than a thin spoon, but still mixed this up with clay always sinking at the last check. At home, try floating a clay ball and then reshaping it into a small bowl, and ask what changed.
